summary: Choose some of many in two lists side by side — what is available, and what is chosen — with buttons that move options across, and optionally an order for what is chosen. A form field.
useWhen: the chosen ORDER means something and must be set — who is asked to approve first, which source is searched first, the columns of an export
the chosen set is long and must be reviewed whole, not as tags that wrap
both sides need to be seen at once: what is left out matters as much as what is in

useInstead.when: a handful chosen from a list, with no order
useInstead.why: one field with tags takes a line, where two lists take a panel; the lists earn their room only for a long selection or an order

useInstead.when: a few options, all visible at once, with no order
useInstead.why: a box per option is one click each and needs no second list

useInstead.when: hundreds of options, found by typing
useInstead.why: these lists do not filter; scrolling hundreds of rows to find one is slower than typing three letters

useInstead.when: choosing rows of a table to act on
useInstead.why: a selection for a bulk action is not a form value — the DataTable pattern's row selection is

composition.note: Pass every option in `options`, in the order Available should list them; `value` is the chosen ones, in their chosen order. Name what the lists hold through `labels` — "Available" and "Selected" become "Everyone" and "Approvers" — and the buttons with them ("Add to approvers"). `isReorderable` when the order is part of the value.
composition.example: <DualListbox label="Approval order" description="Asked in this order. The next is asked if one does not answer in a day." options={people} value={approvers} onChange={setApprovers} isReorderable labels={{ available: 'Everyone', selected: 'Approvers', add: 'Add to approvers', remove: 'Remove from approvers' }} />

label.note: names the field, and both lists with it — "Approval order Available"

description.note: what the choice does; say what the order means when there is one. Replaced by `errorMessage` while `isInvalid` is set

errorMessage.note: shown only while `isInvalid` is set, and read with the chosen list

labels.note: every string it shows or announces: the two lists' names, the four buttons, the empty text, and the announcements after a move

requires: `label` or `aria-label` — the field's name, which each list is named by, then which list it is
`labels.add` and `labels.remove` that name the list they move to, when the lists are renamed — "Add to approvers", not "Add"
guarantees: a `group` named by the label and described by the helper text, holding two `listbox`es, each `aria-multiselectable` and one tab stop

the listbox pattern's recommended multiple selection: ↑ ↓ move and select, Shift+↑ ↓ extend, Ctrl or ⌘ with ↑ ↓ moves without selecting and Space toggles, Ctrl+A picks every option; a click picks one, Shift- and Ctrl-click extend; Home and End go to the ends; typing jumps to a matching label
Enter or a double click moves an option straight across
four icon-only Buttons, each named by `labels` and disabled while there is nothing for it to do
what moved stays picked in the list it moved to, so Move up can follow Add at once
focus stays on the button pressed; when the move leaves it disabled, focus goes to the first option that moved
every move is announced through a `status` region that is always in the page — "2 moved to Selected", "Kwame Mensah, 2 of 4"
a list with nothing in it stays a named, focusable listbox, described by `labels.empty`
`isRequired` and `isInvalid` are `aria-required` and `aria-invalid` on the chosen list, which the error message describes
a disabled option cannot be picked or moved; `isDisabled` disables every option and button
`name` posts each chosen value, in order, as a hidden input
below 30rem of its own width the lists stack, and the buttons turn to point down and up between them; in RTL the lists swap sides and the arrows follow
rows are at least 32px, above the 24px WCAG 2.2 target minimum; in forced colours the picked rows keep an outline
notes: `isReorderable` when the order is part of the value — Move up and Move down beside the chosen list. Without it the value is a set, kept in the order it was chosen.
The buttons act on what is picked in each list, not on where focus is — pick in Available, then press Add.
Picking and choosing are different: an option picked in Available is highlighted to be moved; only the Selected list is the value.

antiPatterns.dont: two Lists or two MultiSelects with buttons between them
antiPatterns.why: the moves, what stays picked, where focus goes and what is announced are the component; hand-built, each is left out

antiPatterns.dont: labels={{ selected: 'Approvers' }} with the buttons left as "Add to selected"
antiPatterns.do: rename the buttons with the list — `add: 'Add to approvers'`
antiPatterns.why: a button that names a list the screen does not show says nothing about where the option goes

antiPatterns.dont: a DualListbox for three or four options
antiPatterns.why: two lists and four buttons to pick among three things is more control than choice

antiPatterns.dont: an order that matters, with `isReorderable` left off
antiPatterns.why: the order is then whatever order they were added in, with no way to change it but removing and adding again
